In response, the Sky Frontier Foundation stated that the flagged transactions do not mean all funds were stolen assets, noting that the volume accounts for less than 0.06% of PSM's over $930 billion in cumulative volume and occurred almost entirely via third-party DEX aggregators rather than Sky's official website, which implements wallet screening. — link

CFTC Chair: Onchain Platforms Like Hyperliquid Must Register or Partner With Licensed Exchanges to Enter US Market, Citing Backpack Model

CFTC Chair Michael Selig said onchain platforms such as Hyperliquid must register as exchanges or partner with registered exchanges to offer derivatives to U.S. retail users. They must follow the same rules as traditional exchanges but may still use onchain technology. He cited Backpack, which recently secured futures commission merchant (FCM), designated contract market (DCM) and derivatives clearing organization (DCO) approvals as a compliance basis for entering the U.S. market.

On prediction markets, Selig said the CFTC would work with the Justice Department to defend its federal authority over lawful derivatives contracts against state lawsuits. He also said a single-stock perpetual contract is not necessarily a security-based swap simply because it has no expiry date: its classification depends on its structure, and perpetual funding rates resemble the variation margin settlement used in traditional futures. — link
